subject: biology

items.q: Do arteries always carry oxygenated blood?
items.correct: No — the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs.
items.misconception: Yes, every artery carries oxygenated blood.
items.random_wrong: Arteries carry no blood at all.
items.why: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; usually oxygenated, but the pulmonary artery is the exception.

items.q: Are breathing and respiration the same thing?
items.correct: No — breathing moves air; respiration releases energy in cells.
items.misconception: Yes, they mean exactly the same.
items.random_wrong: Respiration only happens in the lungs.
items.why: Ventilation (breathing) supplies oxygen; respiration is the chemical reaction releasing energy in every cell.

items.q: How does water enter root hair cells?
items.correct: By osmosis — passively, down a water potential gradient.
items.why: Water moves by osmosis; mineral ions may need active transport against their gradient.

items.q: How many circuits does human blood flow through per cycle?
items.misconception: One single loop around the body.
items.why: Blood passes through the heart twice per full circuit: once to the lungs, once to the body.
